sourceHtml:
This post is co-written with Nick Tamburro of DXC Technology.

When an AI agent can act on a production server at a bank or a hospital, access to a capable foundation model is only the starting point. Recent public incidents, in which autonomous agents took destructive actions their operators never intended, show that the real risk is rarely the model alone. It’s an agent holding more authority than its task requires, with nothing in the architecture to stop it. Avoiding that starts with a substrate that governs model access at the infrastructure level.

Amazon Bedrock provides that substrate. Through a single managed interface, it gives DXC OASIS access to multiple foundation models: Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, and open-weight families. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforce content filtering, personally identifiable information (PII) redaction, and denied-topic policies uniformly across every model. AWS PrivateLink keeps inference traffic within the customer’s virtual private cloud (VPC), and serverless scaling avoids self-managed GPU infrastructure as a failure point. Because these are system-level controls rather than bolt-ons, they gave DXC Technology a governed foundation for what no model layer can deliver on its own: a trusted harness that orchestrates, governs, and audits AI agents across enterprise IT operations at scale.

Model availability varies by AWS Region. See Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock.

DXC Technology runs managed IT services for some of the world’s most regulated organizations: banks, hospitals, and government agencies. With more than 115,000 employees across 70 countries, DXC operates mission-critical systems where resilience and governance are non-negotiable. When DXC set out to build DXC OASIS, the harness for mission-critical IT operations, the team separated the problem into two layers. The first is a governed model substrate built on Amazon Bedrock. The second is the trusted harness built on top: DXC’s own orchestration, governance, and assurance layer.

In this post, we explore how DXC built the resilient, flexible model substrate beneath DXC OASIS on Amazon Bedrock. We also show where DXC drew the line between what the substrate provides and what the harness must provide. Since general availability in March 2026, DXC OASIS has reduced resolution time by 95% on average across 56 measured use cases.

Across every model, customer data stays within the AWS data boundary: prompts and completions are not shared with third-party model providers and are not used to train the underlying foundation models.

“Our customers operate complex, business-critical environments and need both choice and resilience in how they adopt AI. Amazon Bedrock provides access to a broad ecosystem of models with the governance, security, and operational controls required at enterprise scale. That flexibility allows us to use the right model for the right task, adapt as technology evolves, and stay focused on delivering measurable business outcomes for our customers.”

— Dan Gray, President, GIS, DXC Technology

Solution overview

DXC OASIS separates the question of which model from the question of how work gets done. Amazon Bedrock is the substrate: a governed gateway to foundation models (FMs), reachable through one consistent API, with security and networking controls that keep traffic inside the AWS perimeter. The harness is everything DXC builds on top: orchestration across tools and systems, operational context drawn from 60 years of runbooks and escalation logic, policy enforcement, human-oversight gates, and full auditability of every agent action.

The design goals were:

  1. Resilience: No single point of failure at the model layer.
  2. Flexibility: Route each task to the most appropriate model on cost, latency, and capability.
  3. Regulatory sovereignty: Meet the data-handling expectations of regulated tenants.
  4. Safety by design: Bound what every agent can do, so that no action with operational impact runs without policy checks and, where required, human approval.

The main risk DXC designed against was coupling the system to any single provider, framework, or deployment target. The following diagram shows the key AWS services in the DXC DXC OASIS architecture.

Engineers and operators reach the system through Amazon Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer inside the customer’s Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC). The DXC OASIS agent runtime runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in a private subnet. There, a supervisor agent delegates to capability agents that draw on a knowledge base, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Every model call leaves the subnet through a VPC interface endpoint and AWS PrivateLink to reach Amazon Bedrock, so inference traffic doesn’t traverse the public internet. AWS Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM), AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), TLS 1.2, Amazon CloudWatch, VPC Flow Logs, AWS CloudTrail, and OpenTelemetry provide security and observability across every layer.

Figure 1: The DXC OASIS architecture on AWS

Building the DXC OASIS substrate

DXC began building DXC OASIS as a prototype in early 2025. A cross-functional team reached general availability in March 2026, scaling toward 130 customer environments on Amazon EKS with per-tenant namespaces and GitOps rollout. Building the substrate involved the following tasks:

  1. Establish governed, multi-model access through Amazon Bedrock.
  2. Engineer resilience into every layer of the architecture.
  3. Route each workload to the most appropriate model.
  4. Draw the line between the substrate and the harness.

Establish governed, multi-model access through Amazon Bedrock

Every model DXC OASIS uses (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, and open-weight families) is reached through Amazon Bedrock model inference. A provider outage or deprecation therefore becomes a routing decision, not a system rebuild. Uniform access isn’t the same as uniform behavior, however: models differ in capability, response style, and failure modes. Substituting one model for another is an assurance activity as much as a routing change. Before a model enters production routing, the harness (not the API) evaluates it against DXC OASIS task suites. For more information, see Getting started with Amazon Bedrock.

Engineer resilience into every layer

Resilience in DXC OASIS isn’t one control but the compounding of several. The following table summarizes the resilience controls and what each does for DXC OASIS.

Resilience control What it does for DXC OASIS
No single-provider dependency Every model is reached through Amazon Bedrock model inference. A provider outage or deprecation is a routing decision rather than a system rebuild, with the harness assuring behavioral differences between models before a switch goes live.
Serverless model layer Amazon Bedrock is serverless and the Amazon EKS control plane is AWS managed, removing single points of failure.
Scope-of-impact containment Amazon Bedrock Guardrails apply content filters, denied topics, PII filters, and contextual controls consistently regardless of model, containing the scope of any single failure.
Private, encrypted paths Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink keep model traffic off the public internet. TLS 1.2 in transit and AWS KMS at rest protect data.
Elastic capacity Amazon EKS autoscaling with per-tenant namespaces makes onboarding a new tenant a capacity-planning exercise.

Beyond resilience, DXC OASIS also addresses data residency and sovereignty. Regional inference controls and AWS PrivateLink keep inference within approved AWS Regions and off the public internet, meeting the data-handling expectations of regulated tenants.

Route each workload to the most appropriate model

The strategic reason DXC built on Amazon Bedrock is optionality. Because every model sits behind the same API, the team routes each task to the most appropriate model on cost, latency, and capability, and adopts new frontier models as they arrive without re-plumbing the system.

Model choice as a workload decision

Each task’s capability, latency, and cost requirements determine which model it uses, not system constraints.

Intelligent prompt routing – A single serverless endpoint predicts response quality and routes requests between models in the same family. It sends simpler prompts to lower-cost models and complex reasoning to more capable ones. Prompt caching further cuts latency and cost. For more information, see Intelligent prompt routing in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.

Custom model import – With Custom Model Import, the same governance and tooling extend to models that DXC or its clients bring themselves.

Open and closed models together

Amazon Bedrock supports open-weight models alongside proprietary ones, so DXC pairs frontier reasoning with open-weight models a client can adapt and deploy under one set of guardrails.

Draw the line between the substrate and the harness

Every enterprise agent needs six capabilities. Some are substrate capabilities Amazon Bedrock provides directly. Others are things only the harness can provide because they depend on DXC’s operational context and accountability model. This boundary is also where agent safety is won or lost. Guardrails on model inputs and outputs are necessary, but only the harness can limit what an agent is allowed to do. The following table draws that line.

Capability What Bedrock provides What the harness adds
Orchestration A foundational service layer the harness calls, wraps, or extends. Supervisor and capability-agent delegation across tools, systems, and multi-step workflows, built on the open source LangGraph runtime.
Context Knowledge-base infrastructure and prompt caching for retrieval. 60 years of runbooks, escalation logic, and live IT service management (ITSM) data.
Governance AWS IAM, regional inference controls, and tenant-isolated model access. Per-request policy enforcement, persona-based authorization, and field-level constraints.
Guardrails Amazon Bedrock Guardrails: content filters, denied topics, PII filters. Operational-policy enforcement above the substrate filters: tiered knowledge hierarchy, scoped and auditable agent roles, and customer-specific rules on what an agent can act on.
Human oversight Not a substrate function. Four authority tiers (observe, propose, act with approval, act within scope), with every persona starting read-only, plus approval gates and escalation paths.
Assurance Encryption, auditable infrastructure, and VPC Flow Logs. OpenTelemetry traces for every action, each with a unique execution ID, giving end-to-end traceability from intent to action.

How a workload flows through DXC OASIS

To make the architecture concrete, the following use cases come from the DXC OASIS demo environment. The environment is built around AnyCompany Airlines, a fictional mid-sized airline running a hybrid on-premises and AWS estate.

  1. Incident resolution: Diagnose and fix an at-risk production server, from alert to resolution in under 10 minutes.
  2. Problem management: The ITSM agent ranks the top five incident categories and suggests how to reduce each, work that takes 2–3 hours by hand.
  3. Cloud cost analysis: For the AWS cloud engineer, the Metrics agent breaks down a 90-day cost trend by service and region, then investigates spending peaks on request.

The incident-resolution workflow shows how the substrate and the harness work together:

  1. Alert in business terms – A runbook fails to clear disk space on the FlightOps server. The CIO sees the alert as a business risk: Flight Operations scheduling might be affected within 4 hours. At the same moment, the Linux engineer sees the same alert with the technical detail needed to act.
  2. Plan and delegate – The engineer opens AI Assist from the dashboard widget, and the metric carries into the chat as context. A supervisor agent breaks the request into a plan and delegates to capability agents (DXC OASIS Metrics, Linux System, and ITSM), with every model call made through Amazon Bedrock.
  3. Grounded diagnosis – The DXC OASIS Metrics agent confirms the server is 99% full and cites the knowledge base articles behind its answer. The Linux System agent traces the problem to a single 5 GB temporary file.
  4. Human approval – The agent presents its full execution plan, and nothing runs until the engineer confirms it. In this workflow, the agent operates at the act-with-approval tier: it can diagnose freely, but it can’t change the production server without an explicit, recorded approval.
  5. Governed execution – The fix runs, and DXC OASIS records what ran, on which server, who approved it, and when. The audit trail comes from the harness, not from the agent’s own account of what it did.
  6. Learn and observe – The engineer can turn the conversation into a draft knowledge article. The Query Metrics view shows the agent timeline, delegation flow, and token usage behind the answer.

Results

Since reaching general availability in March 2026, DXC OASIS agents now serve 12 operational personas, spanning Linux, Windows, SAP, virtualization, backup and patching, AWS, Azure, and network operations. Across 56 measured use cases, DXC OASIS has reduced resolution time by 95 percent on average. The following table shows representative measurements.

Task Before After Time saved
Filesystem incident 53–90 mins 3–6 mins ~89–97%
Database performance incident 2–3 hours 5–12 mins ~90–97%
Cloud policy validation 4–8 hours 15–30 mins ~88–97%
Patching validation 45–90 mins 5–10 mins ~85–90%
Complex problem management 2–6 days 8–10 mins ~99%

Diagnostic accuracy is 92% or better, validated against senior engineer judgment.

Lessons learned and what comes next

Four architectural decisions proved most valuable:

Separate model choice from orchestration

By keeping model selection, orchestration framework, and deployment target as independent decisions, DXC avoids re-platforming when a layer evolves.

Compound resilience controls

No single control makes the system resilient. The combination of serverless infrastructure, guardrails at the model layer, private networking, and human-oversight gates creates defense in depth.

Draw the substrate-harness line explicitly

Clarity about what the cloud provides versus what you must build avoids both under-engineering (trusting the model to govern itself) and over-engineering (rebuilding capabilities the substrate already offers).

Bound autonomy before you scale it. Every DXC OASIS persona starts read-only, and broader authority is granted deliberately, one tier at a time. Treating autonomy as something granted per task, rather than a default, is what lets DXC put agents in front of production systems with confidence.

Bound autonomy before you scale it

Every DXC OASIS persona starts read-only and broader authority is granted deliberately, one tier at a time. Treating autonomy as something granted per task, rather than a default, is what lets DXC put agents in front of production systems with confidence.

Looking ahead, DXC is evaluating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore alongside the current orchestration layer, and expanding the system to support additional regulated workloads as new frontier models become available through Amazon Bedrock.

Conclusion

In this post, we showed how DXC Technology built DXC OASIS, the harness for mission-critical IT operations, on a governed, multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock. Keeping model reasoning separate from operational orchestration builds resilience, flexibility, and regulatory compliance into the architecture from the start. The payoff is measurable: resolution time is down 95 percent on average across 56 measured use cases. For teams building their own agentic systems, the lesson is to treat the substrate (what Amazon Bedrock provides) and the harness (what you build on top) as separate layers. Decide early which capabilities belong in each. As scrutiny of autonomous AI grows, that clear line, together with bounded, auditable agent authority, is what lets a system earn trust at scale.

To get started with multi-model architectures on Amazon Bedrock, see the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. To learn more about how DXC OASIS applies this architecture to enterprise IT operations, contact DXC Technology.

  3. AWS PrivateLink documentation
  4. DXC OASIS

translation.html:
本文由 DXC Technology 的 Nick Tamburro 共同撰写。

当 AI 智能体能够在银行或医院的生产服务器上执行操作时，能够访问强大的基础模型只是起点。近期发生的公开事件中，自主智能体执行了其操作人员从未打算让它们执行的破坏性操作，这表明真正的风险很少仅在于模型本身，而在于智能体拥有超出任务所需的权限，且架构中没有任何机制能够阻止它。要避免这种情况，首先需要一个在基础设施层面管控模型访问的底座。

Amazon Bedrock 提供了这样的底座。它通过单一托管接口，让 DXC OASIS 能够访问多种基础模型，包括 Anthropic Claude、Amazon Nova、Meta Llama 和开放权重模型系列。Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 在所有模型上一致执行内容过滤、个人身份信息（PII）脱敏和禁止主题策略。AWS PrivateLink 将推理流量保持在客户的虚拟私有云（VPC）内，无服务器扩缩能力则避免了自管 GPU 基础设施成为故障点。由于这些都是系统级控制措施，而非后加的附属功能，它们为 DXC Technology 提供了一个受治理的基础，用于构建任何模型层都无法独立提供的能力：一个可信的运行管控框架，能够在企业 IT 运维中大规模编排、治理和审计 AI 智能体。

模型可用性因 AWS 区域而异。请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 各 AWS 区域支持的模型。

DXC Technology 为世界上一些监管最严格的组织提供托管 IT 服务，包括银行、医院和政府机构。DXC 在 70 个国家拥有超过 115,000 名员工，运营着关键任务系统，韧性和治理是这些系统不可妥协的要求。在着手构建面向关键任务 IT 运维的运行管控框架 DXC OASIS 时，团队将问题分成了两层。第一层是基于 Amazon Bedrock 构建的受治理模型底座。第二层是建立在其上的可信运行管控框架，即 DXC 自己的编排、治理和保障层。

本文将探讨 DXC 如何基于 Amazon Bedrock，为 DXC OASIS 构建具备韧性且灵活的模型底座。我们还将介绍 DXC 如何划分底座提供的能力与运行管控框架必须提供的能力。自 2026 年 3 月正式发布以来，在 56 个已测量的用例中，DXC OASIS 将解决时间平均缩短了 95%。

对于所有模型，客户数据都保留在 AWS 数据边界内：提示词和模型生成的回复不会与第三方模型提供商共享，也不会用于训练底层基础模型。

“我们的客户运营着复杂且对业务至关重要的环境，在采用 AI 时既需要选择空间，也需要韧性。Amazon Bedrock 提供了访问广泛模型生态的途径，并具备企业级规模所需的治理、安全和运维控制能力。这种灵活性使我们能够为合适的任务使用合适的模型，随着技术发展进行调整，并始终专注于为客户交付可衡量的业务成果。”

— Dan Gray，DXC Technology GIS 总裁

解决方案概览

DXC OASIS 将使用哪个模型与如何完成工作这两个问题分开处理。Amazon Bedrock 是底座：它是一个受治理的基础模型（FM）网关，可通过统一的 API 访问，并通过安全和网络控制措施将流量保持在 AWS 边界内。运行管控框架则涵盖 DXC 在其上构建的全部能力：跨工具和系统的编排、源于 60 年运维手册和升级处理逻辑的运维上下文、策略执行、人工监督关卡，以及对每一次智能体操作的完整可审计性。

设计目标如下：

  1. 韧性：模型层不存在单点故障。
  2. 灵活性：根据成本、延迟和能力，将每项任务路由到最合适的模型。
  3. 监管主权：满足受监管租户对数据处理的要求。
  4. 设计内置安全：限定每个智能体能够执行的操作，确保任何会影响运维的操作都必须经过策略检查，并在需要时获得人工批准。

DXC 在设计中主要防范的风险，是系统与任何单一提供商、框架或部署目标产生耦合。下图展示了 DXC DXC OASIS 架构中的关键 AWS 服务。

工程师和运维人员通过 Amazon Route 53，以及位于客户 Amazon Virtual Private Cloud（Amazon VPC） 内的 Application Load Balancer 访问系统。DXC OASIS 智能体运行时在私有子网中的 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS） 上运行。在这里，主管智能体将任务委派给能力智能体，后者会使用知识库、AWS Secrets Manager、Amazon EventBridge 和 Amazon Simple Storage Service（Amazon S3）。每次模型调用都通过 VPC 接口端点和 AWS PrivateLink 离开子网并访问 Amazon Bedrock，因此推理流量不会经过公共互联网。AWS Identity and Access Management（AWS IAM）、AWS Key Management Service（AWS KMS）、TLS 1.2、Amazon CloudWatch、VPC Flow Logs、AWS CloudTrail 和 OpenTelemetry 为各层提供安全性和可观测性。

图 1：AWS 上的 DXC OASIS 架构

构建 DXC OASIS 底座

DXC 于 2025 年初开始构建 DXC OASIS 原型。一个跨职能团队于 2026 年 3 月实现正式发布，在 Amazon EKS 上采用每租户独立命名空间和 GitOps 发布方式，向支持 130 个客户环境的规模扩展。构建底座涉及以下任务：

  1. 通过 Amazon Bedrock 建立受治理的多模型访问。
  2. 在架构的每一层构建韧性。
  3. 将每项工作负载路由到最合适的模型。
  4. 划清底座与运行管控框架的界限。

通过 Amazon Bedrock 建立受治理的多模型访问

DXC OASIS 使用的所有模型（Anthropic Claude、Amazon Nova、Meta Llama 和开放权重模型系列）都通过 Amazon Bedrock 模型推理访问。因此，提供商服务中断或模型弃用会转化为路由决策，而非系统重建。不过，统一访问并不意味着统一行为：各模型在能力、响应风格和失效模式上都有差异。用一个模型替换另一个模型，既是路由变更，也是一项保障工作。在模型进入生产路由之前，由运行管控框架（而非 API）使用 DXC OASIS 任务套件对其进行评估。有关更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 入门。

在每一层构建韧性

DXC OASIS 的韧性并非来自单一控制措施，而是多项措施的叠加。下表概述了韧性控制措施，以及每项措施对 DXC OASIS 的作用。

韧性控制措施 对 DXC OASIS 的作用
不依赖单一提供商 所有模型都通过 Amazon Bedrock 模型推理访问。提供商服务中断或模型弃用会转化为路由决策，而非系统重建；在切换上线前，运行管控框架会针对模型之间的行为差异进行保障验证。
无服务器模型层 Amazon Bedrock 采用无服务器架构，Amazon EKS 控制平面由 AWS 托管，从而消除单点故障。
限制影响范围 无论使用哪个模型，Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 都会一致应用内容过滤器、禁止主题、PII 过滤器和上下文控制措施，限制任何单次故障的影响范围。
私有加密路径 Amazon VPC 和 AWS PrivateLink 使模型流量避开公共互联网。传输时使用 TLS 1.2，静态存储时使用 AWS KMS，以保护数据。
弹性容量 Amazon EKS 自动扩缩容结合每租户独立命名空间，使接入新租户成为一项容量规划工作。

除韧性外，DXC OASIS 还解决了数据驻留和主权问题。区域推理控制和 AWS PrivateLink 将推理保持在获批的 AWS 区域内，并使其避开公共互联网，满足受监管租户对数据处理的要求。

将每项工作负载路由到最合适的模型

DXC 基于 Amazon Bedrock 构建系统的战略原因在于选择空间。由于所有模型都位于同一个 API 之后，团队可以根据成本、延迟和能力，将每项任务路由到最合适的模型，并在新的前沿模型推出时采用它们，而无需重新改造系统的连接方式。

将模型选择视为工作负载决策

每项任务对能力、延迟和成本的要求决定其使用哪个模型，而不是由系统限制决定。

智能提示词路由 – 单个无服务器端点会预测响应质量，并在同一系列的模型之间路由请求。它将较简单的提示词发送给成本较低的模型，将复杂推理任务发送给能力更强的模型。提示词缓存进一步降低延迟和成本。有关更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 文档中的智能提示词路由。

自定义模型导入 – 借助 Custom Model Import，同样的治理能力和工具也可扩展到 DXC 或其客户自行引入的模型。

开放模型与封闭模型协同使用

Amazon Bedrock 同时支持开放权重模型和专有模型，因此 DXC 可以在同一套护栏下，将前沿推理能力与客户能够适配和部署的开放权重模型相结合。

划清底座与运行管控框架的界限

每个企业智能体都需要六项能力。其中一些是 Amazon Bedrock 直接提供的底座能力。另一些则只有运行管控框架才能提供，因为它们依赖 DXC 的运维上下文和问责模式。这一边界也是决定智能体安全成败的关键。模型输入和输出的护栏是必要的，但只有运行管控框架才能限制智能体获准执行的操作。下表划出了这条界限。

能力 Bedrock 提供的能力 运行管控框架补充的能力
编排 供运行管控框架调用、封装或扩展的基础服务层。 基于开源 LangGraph 运行时构建的主管智能体与能力智能体任务委派，覆盖工具、系统和多步骤工作流。
上下文 用于检索的知识库基础设施和提示词缓存。 60 年积累的运维手册、升级处理逻辑，以及实时 IT 服务管理（ITSM）数据。
治理 AWS IAM、区域推理控制，以及租户隔离的模型访问。 逐请求策略执行、基于角色的授权，以及字段级约束。
护栏 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails：内容过滤器、禁止主题、PII 过滤器。 位于底座过滤器之上的运维策略执行：分层知识体系、范围明确且可审计的智能体角色，以及针对智能体可操作对象的客户专属规则。
人工监督 不属于底座功能。 四个权限层级（观察、提议、经批准后执行、在授权范围内执行），所有角色均从只读权限开始，并配有审批关卡和升级处理路径。
保障 加密、可审计的基础设施，以及 VPC Flow Logs。 每项操作均有 OpenTelemetry 跟踪记录，并带有唯一执行 ID，实现从意图到操作的端到端可追溯性。

工作负载如何流经 DXC OASIS

为具体说明这一架构，以下用例取自 DXC OASIS 演示环境。该环境围绕 AnyCompany Airlines 构建，这是一家虚构的中型航空公司，运行着由本地基础设施和 AWS 组成的混合 IT 环境。

  1. 事件解决：诊断并修复存在风险的生产服务器，从告警到解决用时不到 10 分钟。
  2. 问题管理：ITSM 智能体对排名前五的事件类别进行排序，并建议如何减少每一类事件；这项工作手工完成需要 2–3 小时。
  3. 云成本分析：面向 AWS 云工程师，Metrics 智能体按服务和区域拆解 90 天的成本趋势，然后按要求调查支出峰值。

事件解决工作流展示了底座与运行管控框架如何协同工作：

  1. 用业务语言呈现告警 – 一份运维手册未能成功清理 FlightOps 服务器的磁盘空间。CIO 看到的告警呈现为业务风险：航班运行调度可能在 4 小时内受到影响。与此同时，Linux 工程师看到同一条告警，其中包含采取行动所需的技术细节。
  2. 规划与委派 – 工程师从仪表板小组件打开 AI Assist，相关指标随之作为上下文带入聊天。主管智能体将请求拆解为计划，并委派给能力智能体（DXC OASIS Metrics、Linux System 和 ITSM），每次模型调用都通过 Amazon Bedrock 进行。
  3. 有据可依的诊断 – DXC OASIS Metrics 智能体确认服务器空间使用率已达 99%，并引用支撑其回答的知识库文章。Linux System 智能体将问题追溯到一个 5 GB 的临时文件。
  4. 人工批准 – 智能体展示完整执行计划，在工程师确认之前不会执行任何操作。在此工作流中，智能体处于“经批准后执行”层级：它可以自由开展诊断，但没有明确且已记录的批准，就不能更改生产服务器。
  5. 受治理的执行 – 修复开始执行，DXC OASIS 会记录执行了什么、在哪台服务器上执行、由谁批准，以及执行时间。审计轨迹来自运行管控框架，而不是智能体对自身行为的描述。
  6. 学习与观察 – 工程师可以将对话转换为知识文章草稿。Query Metrics 视图会展示生成答案所涉及的智能体时间线、委派流程和 token 使用情况。

经验教训与下一步计划

四项架构决策被证明最有价值：

将模型选择与编排分离

通过将模型选择、编排框架和部署目标保持为相互独立的决策，DXC 避免了某一层演进时必须迁移整个平台。

叠加韧性控制措施

没有任何单一控制措施能够让系统具备韧性。无服务器基础设施、模型层护栏、私有网络和人工监督关卡相结合，形成了纵深防御。

明确划分底座与运行管控框架的界限

明确云服务提供什么、自己必须构建什么，既能避免工程投入不足（相信模型会自行治理），也能避免过度设计（重建底座已经提供的能力）。

在扩大自主能力之前，先限定其边界。DXC OASIS 的每个角色都从只读权限开始，更广泛的权限则经过审慎考量，逐级授予。将自主能力视为按任务授予的权限，而不是默认拥有的能力，正是 DXC 能够放心让智能体接触生产系统的原因。

结论

本文展示了 DXC Technology 如何在 Amazon Bedrock 中受治理的多模型底座之上，构建面向关键任务 IT 运维的运行管控框架 DXC OASIS。将模型推理与运维编排分离，使韧性、灵活性和监管合规从一开始就融入架构。成效可以衡量：在 56 个已测量的用例中，解决时间平均缩短了 95%。对于正在构建自身智能体系统的团队，经验是将底座（Amazon Bedrock 提供的能力）和运行管控框架（你在其上构建的能力）视为独立的两层。尽早决定每项能力归属哪一层。随着自主 AI 受到越来越严格的审视，这条清晰的界限，加上边界明确且可审计的智能体权限，正是系统能够在大规模应用中赢得信任的基础。
